transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hey, yeah, thanks. So, it's kind of a lot to explain, but basically... I work landscaping, right? Just a regular crew guy, mowing, edging, putting down mulch, hauling brush. I've been doing it since right out of high school, just putting my head down and doing the work. But lately, things just got really out of hand, I guess. 

What actually brought me in is that I went from being just a normal crew guy to suddenly trying to run, like, three massive commercial bids all at the exact same time. And I'm not even management! But I was on the phone constantly, calling up city people—like the local zoning department, the parks and rec guys—just leaving them all these messages because I had this huge idea for a community park revamp. I was lining up plant suppliers, getting wholesale quotes on native shrubs and hardscaping materials, trying to coordinate deliveries for land we didn't even have the contract for yet. 

And I was just messaging literally everybody I knew about this park idea. I was texting my buddies, my cousins, guys I haven't talked to in years, just pitching this whole thing over and over, sending them links and sketches. It was like... I don't know, it was like I just couldn’t shut it off. My brain was just locked onto getting all these projects moving and I couldn't stop making the calls and doing the planning, and eventually my boss and my family kind of sat me down and said I needed to come talk to somebody about it.
Can you describe how you were feeling during that time when you were working on all those projects? Were you feeling unusually energetic, excited, or like your thoughts were racing?

Yeah, energetic doesn't even... I mean, it was like I had a motor running inside me that just wouldn't quit. Before I crashed, I just felt completely fired up. Like, totally untouchable. I felt almost bigger than myself, if that makes sense. Like I wasn't just a regular guy pushing a mower or laying sod anymore, I was this, like, visionary who was gonna change the whole city's green spaces. I was so excited about it, just buzzing all day long while we were out on the sites, sketching things out on my breaks, talking a mile a minute. 

But, the thing is, it wasn't just happy excitement. That's what really got me in trouble with the guys on the crew. Because I had all this energy and this huge plan, but if anyone got in my way, it was bad. Like, my buddy Dave, he's been on the crew with me for five years, good guy, usually we joke around while we're hauling brush or whatever. But he was looking at my clipboard one morning, and he just made some offhand comment, like, "Hey man, maybe you need to slow down, you're not the foreman." 

And I just... I completely lost it on him. I snapped at him way, way harder than made sense. I was yelling, telling him he just didn't have the brains to see what I was building. I was just so irritated. And it wasn't just Dave. If any coworker questioned my plan or told me to take a breath or slow down, I felt like they were actively trying to sabotage me, and I'd just bite their head off. I couldn't stand anyone slowing my momentum down, you know? Because I was just so dialed in to this massive project, and I felt like they were all just moving in slow motion and dragging me down. I just had zero patience for anyone who wasn't on my exact wavelength.
